name: desktop-mcp

tools.name: permissions_describe
tools.description: Describe what you are and are not allowed to do on this computer (the active permission policy).

instructions:
Controlled access to the user's computer (linux). Tools: run commands in the native shell (bash/zsh, or PowerShell on Windows), read/write/edit/move/delete files, search files, inspect and kill processes, clipboard, open files/URLs, search the web and (if enabled) see and drive the desktop: mouse, keyboard, windows, OCR, image matching.

A permission policy limits what you may do. Call permissions_describe, or read desktop-mcp://permissions, at the start of any task: it is the authoritative status of what is allowed, requires approval, or is not available. Tools you cannot use are not listed; a call outside the policy is refused with a reason. Work carefully: inspect before changing, verify results after acting, prefer small reversible steps, and use commands that match the host OS (see system_info). Read desktop-mcp://documentation for operational guidance.

# desktop-mcp runtime documentation

desktop-mcp is a local MCP server giving controlled access to the user's computer.
Only tools permitted by the active policy are listed. Use the tool list and the
permissions status as the source of truth.

Feature areas:
- Mouse, keyboard, clipboard and windows.
- Screen capture, OCR, image matching, colour search and recording.
- File, directory, process, shell and system tools.
- Network-limited web tools.

Safe-operation guidance:
- Start with permissions_describe and treat its output as authoritative.
- Inspect before changing; verify after acting.
- Prefer small, reversible steps.
- Respect read-only paths, denied paths and command allow-lists.
- Keep typed text and command payloads short and deliberate.

MCP resources:
- desktop-mcp://documentation
- desktop-mcp://permissions
